name: H-boat (H-vene, H-Boot)
designer: Hans Groop, 1967; class plans of Finlands Seglarförbund / Suomen Purjehtijaliitto (revisions to 1977)

frame.units: SI (m, kg, s, rad in APIs; degrees only where a field name says Deg)
frame.bodyFrame: origin at station 5 on KVL (the construction waterline, CWL); +x forward, +y up, +z starboard; right-handed, y-up like glTF
frame.stations: station s at x = (s − 5) × 0.630 m; station 0 = aft end of KVL, 10 = fore end (LWL 6.300)
frame.drawingDatum: offsets are printed in mm: half-breadths from the centreline, heights from KVL
frame.signs: heel + = starboard down; trim + = bow down; rudder + = trailing edge to port; boomAngle/jibAngle + = to starboard

provenanceFlags.p: printed on a drawing or in the class rules
provenanceFlags.m: measured on a calibrated scan (uncertainty given)

orcComparison.definition: ORC VCG is measured from the flotation waterline in measurement trim, positive up (negative = below WL). VCGD = default/derived value, VCGM = from measured stability (inclining) — here the OD certificate values, not a real inclining.

individualBoats.note: below class minimum, probably measured light

orcComparison._src: ORC, ORCB; dsplSailing ≈ measurement + crew + ~115 kg ORC sailing allowance (d)

massBudget.note: Item masses other than keel are estimates; their sum falls short of the 1450 kg minimum by the corrector total, which the rules place as lead at stations 2 and 8 under the deck. Real boats differ: older/heavier laminates reduce or remove correctors. The keel and rudder rows are placeholders: mass.ts replaces them with the integrated appendage geometry and re-solves the correctors.

crew.positionMeaning: body CG of each person; z>0 = starboard. Hiking: torso outboard of sheer, legs inside rail (footstraps allowed, CR 3.8.4).
